title: Power Automate process mining: Process Intelligence Studio for object-centric models
summary: The briefing is held because the cited PowerShell reference does not document the setting-specific command offered to restrict capacity allocation. The roadmap dates, automatic enablement and descriptions of the analysis workspace are supported.

claims.claim: This roadmap change belongs to Power Automate process mining.
claims.quote: Power Automate: Process mining - Enable Process Intelligence Studio in object-centric process mining

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

The change is enabled automatically for admins, makers and marketers, supporting defaultState on.

claims.where: What's changing, first and last paragraphs
claims.claim: The existing customisable analysis workspace is documented as the process intelligence experience in Power Automate Process Mining.
claims.quote: The new process intelligence experience is the next-generation interface for process analysis in Power Automate Process Mining. It delivers a comprehensive, customizable dashboard for exploring process intelligence insights.

claims.claim: The workspace offers tab-based navigation.
claims.quote: The tab bar organizes your analytical views. It's located at the top of the interface.

claims.claim: Tiles or cards can be arranged in flexible grid layouts.
claims.quote: The main canvas displays multiple cards arranged in a grid layout.

claims.claim: Filters apply across all cards and visualisations on the current tab.
claims.quote: Filters apply to all cards and visualizations on the current tab.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes saved workspace configurations.
claims.quote: Process Intelligence Studio saves your workspace configurations

claims.where: What's changing, first paragraph; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The roadmap describes reusable analysis templates.
claims.quote: allowing teams to create reusable analysis templates

claims.where: What's changing, first paragraph; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The roadmap describes sharing standardised workspace views across teams.
claims.quote: share standardized views across the organization for consistent process monitoring and improvement tracking.

claims.where: summary; What's changing, second paragraph; Why it matters
claims.claim: The roadmap plans to extend full Process Intelligence Studio functionality to OCPM models.
claims.quote: Object-centric support: Extends full functionality to OCPM models, enabling multi-dimensional analysis of interconnected objects, relationships, and cross-object metrics within the same intuitive interface.

claims.claim: The planned workspace supports traditional case-centric and object-centric process models.
claims.quote: The platform supports both traditional and object-centric process mining methodologies, enabling analysis across simple linear processes and complex, multi-object scenarios.

claims.claim: An OCPM event can relate to several objects, including orders, invoices and payments.
claims.quote: OCPM lets one event belong to multiple objects (and object types), keeping the full context intact.

claims.where: What's changing, second paragraph; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: OCPM models can be created from an object-centric event log stored in Azure Data Lake Gen2.
claims.quote: To access OCPM (object-centric process mining) in Power Automate Process Mining, first create a process model by ingesting the object-centric event log (OCEL). ... Then, store the resulting file in a CSV format in either Azure Data Lake Gen2 or OneLake.

claims.where: What's changing, second paragraph; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The object-centric event log can alternatively be stored in OneLake.
claims.quote: Then, store the resulting file in a CSV format in either Azure Data Lake Gen2 or OneLake.

claims.claim: The documented OCPM preview makes only the Process overview tab available.
claims.quote: In the preview of this feature, only the Process overview tab is available.

claims.claim: The documented OCPM preview makes only the Default view available.
claims.quote: In the preview of this feature, only the Default view is available.

claims.claim: Object-centric event logs can contain order and invoice identifiers.
claims.quote: In OCPM, you work with object-centric event data where each row is an event (with activity and timestamp) and has one or more columns listing the object IDs per object type that the event touched (for example, Order=O2, Invoice=I1).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; controls[2].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Process mining access is governed by environment security and process-related Dataverse permissions.
claims.quote: The process mining capability relies on environment security and Microsoft Dataverse security roles and privileges to grant access to its features in Power Automate.

claims.claim: Learn documents the Environment Maker role for creating processes.
claims.quote: You need the Environment Maker role to create, share, and contribute to processes.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The roadmap describes an analysis workspace over process data rather than introducing an autonomous automation capability.
claims.quote: Process Intelligence Studio is a modern, flexible workspace designed for comprehensive process analysis. It provides a fully customizable analysis environment that combines multiple visualization and analysis components into cohesive, purpose-built workspaces.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Additional licensing specific to this workspace change is not yet published, so the incremental licensing model is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: "Process Intelligence Studio" licensing; "object-centric" "licensing" "Power Automate"; "process intelligence experience" "license". Opened process-advisor-overview, process-mining-studio-overview and object-centric-ingest-event-log; no change-specific licence terms.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Power Automate process mining has documented baseline licensing that remains relevant to its use.
claims.quote: Process mining is licensed as part of Microsoft Power Automate. Three Power Automate licenses relate to process mining, and a Power BI license is required for Power BI report customization.

claims.claim: Azure Data Lake storage used for the event log carries storage cost.
claims.quote: To analyze differences in data storage prices, transaction prices, and storage capacity reservation pricing between accounts that have a flat namespace versus a hierarchical namespace, see Azure Data Lake Storage pricing.

claims.claim: OneLake storage used for the event log carries storage cost.
claims.quote: Storage charges: The per-GB, per-month cost that's highest for hot storage and lowest for cold storage.

claims.claim: Power Automate Premium licences contribute process mining capacity.
claims.quote: Each Power Automate Premium license adds 50 MB of process mining capacity to a tenant-wide capacity pool up to a total of 100 GB.

claims.claim: The Power Automate Process Mining add-on contributes additional process mining capacity.
claims.quote: The Process Mining add-on is a tenant-wide license that's available for the Power Automate Premium license. It offers: An extra 100 GB of process mining capacity to the capacity pool

claims.claim: Process mining capacity is pooled tenant-wide.
claims.quote: Each Power Automate Premium license adds 50 MB of process mining capacity to a tenant-wide capacity pool up to a total of 100 GB.

claims.claim: A process-mining-specific capacity allocation path in the admin UI is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "process mining" "capacity" "admin center" allocate; "process mining capacity" "allocate". Opened capacity-add-on and programmability-tutorial-allocate-capacity-addons; generic UI paths, but no explicit Process Mining allocation UI.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table and closing paragraph
claims.claim: PATCH https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/environments/{environmentId}/allocations?api-version=2024-10-01 with currencyAllocations containing currencyType ProcessMiningDataStorage and allocated sets environment process mining capacity.
claims.quote: PATCH https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/environments/{environmentId}/allocations?api-version=2024-10-01; currencyAllocations | CurrencyAllocationRequestModelV1[]; allocated | integer (int32); currencyType | ExternalCurrencyType; ProcessMiningDataStorage

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Settings > Power Platform settings > Tenant settings > Add-on capacity assignments > Only specific admins restricts capacity allocation at tenant scope.
claims.quote: In the title bar, select the Settings icon. Select Power Platform settings. On the Tenant settings page, select Add-on capacity assignments, and then select Only specific admins.

claims.claim: The linked Set-TenantSettings reference documents Set-TenantSettings -RequestBody @{disableCapacityAllocationByEnvironmentAdmins=$true} as the automation equivalent of the capacity-assignment restriction.
claims.quote: Searched: "Set-TenantSettings" "disableCapacityAllocationByEnvironmentAdmins". Opened Set-TenantSettings and list-tenantsettings: the reference documents -RequestBody but not this key; the preview list defines the key but does not document this PowerShell call.
claims.fix: Set controls[1].api to null and remove its rendered PowerShell call. Replace the row note with 'The preview list-tenantsettings documentation defines disableCapacityAllocationByEnvironmentAdmins, but the Set-TenantSettings reference does not document a PowerShell call for this setting.' Retain the verified UI path.

claims.claim: The tenant-setting definition is on a Learn page marked preview.
claims.quote: List tenant settings (preview). This article is prerelease documentation and is subject to change.

claims.where: controls[2].ui and api; Governance controls table and closing paragraph
claims.claim: A separate admin UI or automation switch for Process Intelligence Studio or object-centric models is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Process Intelligence Studio" "enable"; "object-centric" "process mining" "disable"; "process mining" "studio" "pac admin" "Power Platform API" enable. Opened studio overview, OCPM ingestion and list-tenantsettings; no feature switch.

claims.claim: Event-log storage introduces access requirements in addition to Power Automate environment roles.
claims.quote: all users that have the Owner or Co-Owner role on the process must be attributed: Storage Blob Data Reader or Storage Blob Data Contributor role assigned; Azure Resource Manager Reader role assigned, at minimum.

claims.claim: The allocating-add-ons programmability tutorial shows allocation through a Power Automate flow.
claims.quote: Allocate an add-on using Power Automate flows or Logic Apps. Add a new action to the canvas, searching for "Allocate and deallocate the currencies for the environment".

claims.claim: Process analysts and process owners are intended users of the planned workspace.
claims.quote: Business analysts, process owners, and improvement teams can now build comprehensive views that tell the complete story
